summary: Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was a doctoral student at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Berlin State Library around 1989.

Michael Baxandall studied at Downing College (~1951–1954). He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (1961–1965), Warburg Institute (~1965–1986), Cornell University (~1982–1987), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1986–1996).

Michael Carrithers works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford in 1977 and served as Lecturer in Social Anthropology at Durham University from around 1982 to 1992.

Philosopher Michael Chase studied at the University of Victoria (~1977–1985) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1990–1997). Around 1999, he became a researcher in ancient philosophy at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Michael Comans works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University (~1984–1987), later holding posts at the University of Sydney (~1989–2000) and Sri Venkateswara Temple.

Michael Como specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under advisers Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt (~1995–2000), as well as Kuo-liang Wang, and held a post at Columbia University around 2004.

Michael D. Willis studied at the University of Victoria (~1973–1977) and the University of Chicago (~1977–1986). His career includes posts at UBC, SUNY New Paltz, the British Museum (1994–2015), De Montfort University, and the European Research Council (2014–2020).
Michael Friedrich is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Succeeding Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, he was appointed professor at the University of Hamburg around 1994.

Michael G. Morony studied at UC Berkeley (~1957–1961) and UCLA (~1961–1971), working in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from around 1974 to 2015.

Michael Hahn studied under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1967) and Bonn. He held posts at Bonn, Marburg (~1988–2006), the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, Ryukoku University (~1997–1998), and SOAS (~2003–2004).
Michael Harack studied religious studies and Sinology at McMaster University, completing his Master of Arts around 2005–2007 under the supervision of James A. Benn, Mark Rowe, and Shayne Clarke.

Michael Hookham, working in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa (1965–1987), Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche. He founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at SOAS University of London (~1976–1984) and completed his doctorate at the University of London (~1980–1984), later serving as Lecturer in Nepali at SOAS (~1987–2021).

Michael J. Sweet studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. ~1968–1977) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Richard Hugh Robinson, Ngawang Legden, Geshe Wangyal, and Khenpo Sangye Tenzin, later becoming clinical Assistant Professor in Psychiatry there.

Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He earned a Master of Arts at San Diego State University (~2008–2011), studying under supervisor Sandra A. Wawrytko and committee member Sthaneshwar Timalsina.

Michael J. Walsh studied at the University of Cape Town (~1987–1990) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2000) under doctoral supervisor William F. Powell, specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology.

Michael K. Jerryson studied at UW-Madison and UC Santa Barbara (PhD ~2003–2008 under Mark Juergensmeyer). He worked in Buddhist and religious studies, holding posts at Eckerd College (~2010–2013) and Youngstown State University (~2013–2021).
Michael Kowalewski works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter, working in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied under Larry Moses. He has held posts as a Special Languages Cataloger at Indiana University and as a Research Fellow at Lumbini International Research Institute.
Michael M. Broido, a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Cambridge and later held a post at the University of Oxford.
